{{Short description|Saudi businessman (born 1970)}} {{Use dmy dates|date=June 2023}} {{Use British English|date=June 2023}} {{Infobox officeholder | name = Yasir Al-Rumayyan | office = Chairman of [[Newcastle United F.C.]] | image = Yasir Al-Rumayyan Argentina v Spain 19 July 2026-285.jpg | caption = Al-Rumayyan in 2026 | native_name = {{Nobold|ياسر الرميان}} | birth_name = Yasir bin Othman Al-Rumayyan | birth_date = {{birth date and age|1970|2|18|df=yes}} | birth_place = [[Buraidah]], Saudi Arabia | bodyclass = | term_start = 19 November 2021 | office2 = Governor of [[Public Investment Fund]] | term_start2 = September 2015 | title = | 1blankname = Co-owners | 1namedata = [[Amanda Staveley]] (2021–2024)
[[Jamie Reuben|RB Sports & Media]] (2021–) | 2blankname = Head coaches | 2namedata = {{plainlist| * [[Steve Bruce]] (2021) * [[Eddie Howe]] (2021–26) * TBA }} | education = [[King Faisal University]] | occupation = Businessman | native_name_lang = ar | predecessor = Lee Charnley }} '''Yasir bin Othman Al-Rumayyan''' ({{langx|ar|ياسر الرميان}}; born 18 February 1970) is a Saudi Arabian [[Businessperson|businessman]] who is governor of the [[Public Investment Fund]] (PIF), the [[sovereign wealth fund]] of the [[Kingdom of Saudi Arabia]]. He is currently the chairman of [[Newcastle United F.C.|NUFC]] since 2021. He also chairs the state-owned petroleum company [[Saudi Aramco]] and Saudi Arabia's largest [[mining]] company [[Ma'aden (company)|Ma'aden]].{{Cite news |last=Whitehead |first=Jacob |title=Yasir Al-Rumayyan: A life of power, privilege and risk for golf's most powerful man |date=29 March 2023|access-date=17 March 2025|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/4343985/2023/03/29/yasir-al-rumayyan-newcastle-profile/ |work=[[The New York Times]]|url-access=subscription |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}} He is chairman of the English football club [[Newcastle United]] and manages the [[LIV Golf]] professional men's golf tour. He is chairman of [[Riyadh Air]]. He is also involved in the construction of [[Neom]], a controversial megaproject. Al-Rumayyan is a close ally of Saudi ruler [[Mohammed bin Salman]]. His early career was in finance. When King Abdullah died in 2015 and power consolidated around Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, Al-Rumayyan was appointed chairman of PIF and placed on the board of Saudi Aramco. After Bin Salman's [[2017–2019 Saudi Arabian purge|2017 purge]] of competing Saudi political elites, Al-Rumayyan and his associates assisted Bin Salman in consolidating his authority, while the sovereign fund acquired assets seized from prominent Saudi figures. == Early life and education == Yasir Al-Rumayyan was born in [[Buraidah]], [[Al-Qassim Province]], in 1970. His parents were both from Saudi Arabia. He moved to Riyadh as a child, where he attended Al-Abna'a. He graduated from [[King Faisal University]] in [[Al-Ahsa Governorate|Alahsa]] in 1993 with a degree in accounting. He did a three-month course at [[Harvard Business School]] in 2007. == Career == He began his career at [[Saudi Hollandi Bank]], becoming head of international brokerage before joining the [[Capital Market Authority of Saudi Arabia|Capital Markets Authority]] (CMA), where he was head of securities listings.{{cite web |url=https://www.thebusinessyear.com/saudi-arabia-2014/all-transactions-go/interview |title=All transactions go |author= |date=June 2014 |website=The Business Year |access-date=25 June 2019 |archive-date=7 January 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220107144005/https://www.thebusinessyear.com/saudi-arabia-2014/all-transactions-go/interview |url-status=dead }}{{cite web |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/saudi-fransi-jallal/banque-saudi-fransi-loses-key-equity-banker-to-jadwa-investment-idUKL6N0M03G020140306 |title=Banque Saudi Fransi loses key equity banker to Jadwa Investment |author=David French |work=[[Reuters]] |date=6 March 2014}} Between 2011 and 2015, Al-Rumayyan was CEO of Saudi Fransi Capital (SFC), the investment banking arm of [[Banque Saudi Fransi]].{{cite web |url=https://www.arabnews.com/node/1299771/saudi-arabia |title=FaceOf: Yasir Al-Rumayyan, head of the Saudi Public Investment Fund |author= |date=9 May 2018 |website=[[Arab News]]}}{{cite news |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/moves-fransi-rumayyan/moves-ceo-of-saudi-fransi-capital-resigns-source-idINL5N0VX3H220150223 |title=MOVES-CEO of Saudi Fransi Capital resigns - source |author= |website=[[Reuters]] |date=23 February 2015}} From 2014 to 2015 he was on the board of directors of the [[Saudi Stock Exchange]]. Al-Rumayyan sits on the boards of [[SoftBank Group]] and [[Reliance Industries|Reliance Industries Ltd]].{{Cite news |title=Saudi Aramco chairman Yasir Al-Rumayyan joins Reliance Industries Board |newspaper=The Economic Times |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/company/corporate-trends/saudi-aramco-chairman-yasir-al-rumayyan-joins-reliance-industries-board/articleshow/83804716.cms}} Al-Rumayyan was made chairman of the Saudi Aramco board in September 2019 after Crown Prince Bin Salman stripped [[Khalid A. Al-Falih|Khalid Al-Falih]], the energy minister, of his duties when he questioned Bin Salman's directives. === Public Investment Fund === In September 2015, Al-Rumayyan was appointed managing director of the [[Public Investment Fund of Saudi Arabia]] (PIF).{{cite web |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-saudi-economy-funds-borrowing/huge-saudi-fund-to-be-conservative-borrower-chief-says-idUSKBN1CU2CY |title=Huge Saudi fund to be conservative borrower, chief says |author=Andrew Torchia |work=[[Reuters]] |date=25 October 2017}}{{cite web |url=http://live.saudigazette.com.sa/article/141311/KSA-keen-on-overseas-buying-with-potential-for-knowledge-transfer |title=KSA keen on overseas buying with potential for knowledge transfer |author= |date=28 October 2015 |website=[[Saudi Gazette]] |access-date=25 June 2019 |archive-date=7 January 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220107144028/https://live.saudigazette.com.sa/article/141311/KSA-keen-on-overseas-buying-with-potential-for-knowledge-transfer |url-status=dead }} In 2016, PIF invested $3.5 billion in the US-based [[Uber]].{{cite web |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/alexkonrad/2016/06/01/uber-raises-3-5-billion-from-saudi-sovereign-fund-at-62-5-billion-valuation/#7b9d711f78d9 |title=Uber Raises $3.5 Billion From Saudi Sovereign Wealth Fund, Keeps $62.5 Billion Valuation |author=Alex Konrad |work=[[Forbes]] |date=1 June 2016}} He joined Uber's board of directors as part of the agreement.{{cite web |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/uber-saudi-funds-idUSL8N18U2QN |title=Saudi signals new investment strategies in $3.5 bln Uber deal |author= |date=2 June 2016 |website=[[Reuters]]}} In August 2016, Al-Rumayyan joined the board of the state oil company [[Saudi Aramco]] as part of a move toward closer cooperation between Aramco and PIF in restructuring the Saudi economy.{{cite web |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/saudi-aramco-board/saudi-aramco-appoints-chief-of-sovereign-wealth-fund-to-board-idUSL8N1AR4XZ |title=Saudi Aramco appoints chief of sovereign wealth fund to board |author= |date=10 August 2016 |website=[[Reuters]]}} In October that year, PIF invested $45 billion in the newly established [[SoftBank Vision Fund]].{{cite web |url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/softbank-saudis-to-launch-100-billion-tech-fund-1495270854 |title=SoftBank, Saudis Launch $100 Billion Tech Fund |author1=Margherita Stancati |author2=Mayumi Negishi |author3=Nicolas Parasie |work=[[The Wall Street Journal]] |date=20 May 2017}} In May 2017, PIF invested $20 billion to a joint US infrastructure fund with [[The Blackstone Group|Blackstone]].{{cite web |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-saudi-economy-pif/saudis-pif-commits-20-bln-to-40-billion-fund-with-blackstone-idUSKBN1CT0RG |title=Saudi's PIF commits $20 bln to $40 billion fund with Blackstone |author= |date=24 October 2017 |website=[[Reuters]]}} Al-Rumayyan was involved in the transfer of assets to PIF in the wake of the Saudi Arabian government's 2017 purge.{{Cite web|date=2021-10-16|title=Revealed: Newcastle chairman's links to Saudi 'anti-corruption' drive|url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2021/oct/16/revealed-newcastle-chairmans-links-to-saudi-anti-corruption-drive|access-date=2021-10-17|website=the Guardian|language=en}} He transferred 20 companies that had been seized by the government into the PIF, including one later alleged to be used by Saudi operatives in the murder of journalist [[Jamal Khashoggi]].{{Cite news |last=Crafton |first=Adam |date=2024 |title=Newcastle chairman Al-Rumayyan faces $74m lawsuit for 'carrying out' malicious instructions of Bin Salman |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/5197880/2024/01/16/newcastle-united-al-rumayyan-pif/ |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}} In October 2021, PIF announced that the acquisition of [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]] by the consortium consisting of the Public Investment Fund and that Al-Rumayyan would be elected as chairman of the club after PIF acquired it.{{cite web|url=https://www.nufc.co.uk/news/latest-news/pif-pcp-capital-partners-and-rb-sports-media-acquire-newcastle-united-football-club/ |title=PIF, PCP Capital Partners and RB Sports & Media acquire Newcastle United Football Club |access-date=7 October 2020 |website=Newcastle United}} == Personal life == He has at least one son. Bin Salman gave Al-Rumayyan a house worth 250 million Saudi riyals (over $60m) near the presidential palace. He has been described as passionate about golfing. After Bin Salman's purge of other Saudi political elites, Al-Rumayyan's brother-in-law, Mazin bin Ibrahim Al-Kahmous, was made president of Saudi Arabia's Oversight and Anti-Corruption Authority. He is close with [[Donald Trump]] and has been photographed wearing a ‘Make America Great Again’ hat. After Trump's win in the [[2024 United States presidential election|2024 election]], he was spotted at a UFC event in [[Madison Square Garden]] with the president-elect.{{Cite news|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/2024/11/17/donald-trump-pga-liv-golf/|title=Donald Trump has separate meetings with PGA commissioner, Saudi executive|newspaper=Washington Post|date=November 17, 2024}} == References == {{Reflist}} {{commons category}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Rumayyan, Yasir}} [[Category:1970 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:Newcastle United F.C. directors and chairmen]] [[Category:Saudi Arabian businesspeople]] [[Category:SoftBank people]] [[Category:Uber people]] [[Category:King Faisal University alumni]]
